title: M2 Wear engine: WEAR_TABLE + pure functions + pytest (never cut)
description: engine/wear.py with spec wear table verbatim; midpoint scoring, range for display, wet multiplier shortens interval; baselines w/ conservative 'not sure' defaults; bike-type filtering; health score in engine/report.py; tests/test_wear.py.

title: Deploy to Vercel: vercel.json, deploy, verify live link end-to-end
description: Static frontend build + api/index.py as Python function; /api/* rewrite; verify sample-data flow on live URL at phone viewport.

title: M5 Polish: sample-data button (non-negotiable), CSV error handling, empty states, favicon, name
description: Try-with-sample-data loads bundled CSV; friendly errors for missing cols/empty/non-Strava CSV/zero rides; empty states; favicon; product name.

title: M4 Shop Work Order: print-styled checklist view
description: Overdue + due-soon items with checkboxes, bike type, mileage summary, date. @media print CSS, Print/Share button. 'Show this to your shop.'

title: M3 Report UI: 3-question form + urgency-sorted component cards, mobile-first
description: Form: bike type, conditions, optional last-replaced (chain/tires) with 'not sure'. Report: health score header, cards sorted overdue->due-soon->green, usage vs range, plain-language explanations.

title: M1 Scaffold: Vite React TS app, CSV drop zone + Papaparse, FastAPI skeleton
description: Vite react-ts app in frontend/; drop zone; parse only date/type/distance/moving-time/gear cols, filter to rides, km->mi, s->h. FastAPI stub POST /api/report in api/index.py; requirements.txt.

title: Press release: PRESS_RELEASE.md per spec skeleton
description: Write after M3, before M5. 60-seconds headline, problem, 3-step solution, why local shops win, roadmap (iOS+HealthKit, Garmin/Wahoo, shop-side view).

title: Assumption: one tires baseline covers front and rear; single bike per report
description: engine/report.py: baselines.tires_* applies to both tires_front and tires_rear (they're usually replaced separately in reality). Gear column is parsed but unused — all rides count toward one bike (multiple bikes is an explicit v0 cutline).

title: Assumption: ride filter = Ride/Gravel Ride/Mountain Bike Ride/E-Bike Ride; Virtual Ride excluded; Strava distances are km
description: frontend/src/lib/parseActivities.ts RIDE_TYPES: Virtual Ride (trainer) excluded — trainer miles do wear the chain but not tires/brakes; v0 excludes them entirely. Distance column assumed km (Strava export default), converted at 0.621371. Rows with unparseable date/distance/time are silently dropped.

title: Assumption: health score = uniform-weight mean of per-component remaining life
description: engine/report.py: score = 100 * mean(clamp(1 - pct_used, 0, 1)). No component weighting (a worn chain counts the same as bar tape); overdue clamps at 0 so extra overshoot doesn't drag further. Spec doesn't define the formula.

title: Assumption: time-based wear runs from first ride in history to today
description: engine/report.py: bar tape / cables / sealant / safety check use months_between(first_ride, as_of=today), months = days/30.44. Long histories make all time-based items overdue; sealant especially (3-4mo interval).

comments.author: Holly French
comments.text: Partially addressed post-M2: optional bike_date baseline caps time-based wear at the bike's acquisition/service date (commit a0d437c). Default without bike_date is still full-history-conservative.

title: Assumption: 'not sure' and untracked components assume wear over the entire ride history
description: engine/report.py _miles_used(): chain/tires without a baseline, and ALL other mileage components (cassette, pads, BB, chainrings), use total history miles — i.e. never replaced. Conservative per spec, but a 10-year Strava history marks everything overdue. Consider capping or asking about recent service.

comments.author: Holly French
comments.text: Partially addressed post-M2: bike_date baseline excludes previous-bike rides from all wear. Untracked mileage components still assume no replacement since bike_date.

title: Assumption: status thresholds — due-soon at 75% of midpoint, overdue at 100%
description: engine/wear.py DUE_SOON_THRESHOLD=0.75. Spec defines green/due-soon/overdue but not the cutoffs. Midpoint of condition-adjusted range per spec; the 75% knee is our choice.

title: Assumption: mixed conditions = halfway between dry and wet multiplier
description: engine/wear.py condition_multiplier(): spec only defines a wet multiplier; 'mixed' is interpolated as (1.0 + wet_mult)/2. Not from the spec.

title: Assumption: road = rim pads, gravel/MTB = disc pads
description: engine/wear.py WEAR_TABLE: no brake-type question in the 3-question flow, so brake pad intervals are picked by bike type (road->rim 1500-3000mi, gravel/MTB->disc 3000-6000mi). Wrong for disc road bikes (increasingly common) and rim MTB/gravel. Revisit: add a 4th question or a toggle.
